title: delegation.v1 — the per-dispatch token a worker presents as the person it acts for
description: agent-api mints one token per worker dispatch; identity's /internal/validate verifies it and answers with the person it names plus the dispatch's ceiling (identity.v1 ValidateResponse.delegation). Wire form: "vxd_" + base64url(header JSON) + "." + base64url(claims JSON) + "." + base64url(HMAC-SHA256(key, base64url(header) + "." + base64url(claims))). Both JSON documents are canonical: keys sorted at every depth, no whitespace, ASCII-escaped. base64url is unpadded. The key is the symmetric VEXA_MCP_DELEGATION_SECRET, which agent-api (mint) and admin-api (verify) both hold; an empty key is refused on both sides. A verifier checks, in this order: the vxd_ prefix (else not_delegated), three parts (else malformed), the signature in constant time (else bad_signature), that the claims decode to an object (else malformed), aud = vexa-mcp (else bad_audience), a non-empty sub (else malformed), now < exp (else expired), and, only if it keeps a denylist, jti (else revoked). No claim is read before the signature verifies.

Regime.description: human: a person is in the loop this turn (unit.v1 trigger `message`). autonomous: a schedule, an event or a transcription fired it and nobody is watching (every other trigger).

Scope.description: The dispatch's ceiling, never a grant: it narrows what the account can already reach. `workspaces` is "*" (everything already the person's) or the isolation set, sorted and de-duplicated. An autonomous dispatch always carries an explicit set; the minter refuses autonomous with "*".

sub.description: the person's identity user id, resolved by agent-api from the dispatch and never asserted by the worker

aud.description: the audience pin: the token is for the MCP edge and its re-entry, nothing else

exp.description: expires at, unix seconds; valid while now < exp. agent-api mints with a 3600 s lifetime

jti.description: a random id, so a verifier that keeps a denylist can strike one token off

target.description: the chat's target workspace: the slug a workspace verb with no slug of its own defaults to. A default, never a grant, so it is outside `scope`. Absent when there is none

RefusalReason.description: Why a verifier refused a token. Safe to show a caller: it names the failure class, never the token or the key. identity answers 401 "Invalid delegation: <reason>" for every reason but not_delegated, which sends the bearer to the API-key lookup instead.

Vector.description: A minting vector. Minting for subject, regime, workspaces, target and ttl_sec at now with jti and secret must produce `token` exactly (HMAC is deterministic), and `token` must decode to `header` and `claims`. The secret is published test data and authenticates nothing.

Refusal.description: A refusal vector: verifying `token` with `secret` at `now` (and the `revoked` denylist, when given) must fail with `reason`.
